context: Add a read-only 'doctor' to the project wrapper reporting the four things bootstrap.md names: backend/config, identity, database reachability, and auth, plus an advisory turso-CLI check. Run it before connect/freeze so it can diagnose an unreachable or frozen backend. Reserve exit 4 for auth failures (including the real 'JWT error: InvalidToken' shape) and exit 2 for everything else, so batch can distinguish halt-worthy auth from a plain outage. Never print the DSN or the token.
description: The todo-db batch workflow requires a side-effect-free 'doctor' preflight before the first claim, and HALTS on its exit 4 so a dead token cannot desynchronize the tracker from the work. No reachable CLI implements it. Confirmed by enumeration on both surfaces, not a lookup failure: '_project/scripts/todo --help' advertises no 'doctor' (nor 'batch'), and no standalone todo-db exists on this machine at all ('todo-db' and 'todo' absent from PATH, nothing in ~/.local/bin, no pipx entry, todo_db module not importable). So sessions record the mandated gate as 'skipped', quietly turning a required preflight into an optional one. bootstrap.md documents doctor as a todo-db >= 0.3 command, but it is NOT in the skill's standalone_only_commands (only 'update' is), and this wrapper already owns the sibling 'init', so implementing it here is within the boundary. Supersedes the dropped todo-batch-mandates-a-doctor-preflight-that-does-not-exist.

preserves.behavior: Neither the hosted DSN nor the auth token is ever printed, matching _report_backend
No change to the standalone-only command boundary: 'update' stays standalone-only and is not added to the wrapper
doctor performs no tracker write and emits no audit event

work_units.evidence: Decided doctor belongs on this wrapper: bootstrap.md documents it as a todo-db >= 0.3 command, but it is NOT in the skill's standalone_only_commands (only 'update' is), and this wrapper already owns the sibling 'init', so rule 4 is not engaged. Implemented run_doctor() with the four checks bootstrap.md names (backend/config, identity, reachability, auth) plus an advisory turso-CLI check, dispatched from a new _preconnect_command() BEFORE connect/freeze so it can diagnose an unreachable, unmigrated or frozen backend. work_units.evidence: 10 guards in tests/unit/scripts/test_todo_db_doctor.py. Exercising the branches against the live hosted DB caught three real defects in my own first cut, all fixed and pinned: (1) a rejected token returned exit 2, not 4 -- the transport says 'JWT error: InvalidToken' with no space, so an 'invalid token' marker missed it and a batch would have kept running against a dead token instead of halting; (2) the AUTH remediation printed ABOVE the check table when redirected (stdout block-buffered vs unbuffered stderr); (3) _redacted scrubs the token but NOT the DSN, so a transport error quoting the URL leaked it, violating the module's own _report_backend invariant. Verified exit codes: no token 4, bad token 4, plain outage 2, healthy 0. Read-only proven by table+event-count snapshot equality. Full tests/unit/scripts suite 1297 passed, ruff clean, lint-imports/lint-markers/timing-policy green.
work_units.summary: Pin auth-vs-outage classification, read-only behaviour, and DSN/token non-leakage
